entries.clue: Second husband beset by awful pain beginning to emerge healthy (2,5)

indicators.note: the S and H are surrounded by the other letters
PAIN in a terrible state is rearranged
take only the first letter of 'emerge'

blocks.note: PAIN plus E, the start of 'emerge', rearranged

annotation.surface: A woman on her second marriage suffers terrible pain yet somehow comes out of it healthy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second husband' reads as a remarriage, but it is two abbreviations side by side. The enumeration (2,5) is what shows where the pair sits in the shuffled letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone in good physical condition is described as in shape.

entries.clue: One mobilising about pit is type proposed for office (7)

indicators.note: setting ONE in motion moves its letters around
the rearranged letters go around the pit

annotation.surface: Someone rallying support around a coal pit, pictured as a candidate for public office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mobilising' suggests rallying people, but it only sets the three letters of 'One' moving.
annotation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person put forward for a post.

entries.clue: Movable joint is put in something easily (5)

indicators.note: the answer is lodged inside the following words

blocks.note: the last four letters of 'something' plus the first of 'easily'

annotation.surface: A joint that can be moved is fitted into something without much effort.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles two words: somet[HING E]asily. 'Movable joint' sounds anatomical, but a door hinge fits just as well.
annotation.definitionFit: A hinge is a joint that lets a door or lid swing.

entries.clue: Eccentric temping gets natural colouring matter (7)

indicators.note: an eccentric version of TEMPING has its letters out of order

annotation.surface: An odd temporary worker acquires some natural colouring.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' reads as describing a person doing temp work; here it only tells you to rearrange the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Pigment is the substance that gives skin, plants or paint their colour.

entries.clue: Classify businessman’s first dishonest scheme (7)

indicators.note: take only the opening letter of 'businessman'

blocks.note: a racket is a dishonest scheme

annotation.surface: Someone labels a businessman's first shady scheme for what it is.
annotation.walkthrough: To bracket things is to group them together into a class.
annotation.definitionFit: To bracket items is to put them in the same category.

entries.clue: Manage area in wide yard as feature of an airport (6)

indicators.note: the A sits inside W and Y

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
w = wide, a cricket scoring abbreviation

annotation.surface: Someone manages a patch of ground inside a broad yard, as if planning an airport.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wide' looks like an adjective for the yard; it is the cricket term for a ball bowled out of reach, abbreviated W on scorecards.
annotation.definitionFit: A runway is the strip where aircraft take off and land.

entries.clue: Richard shortly entering Crete for recreation is one playing on a square (9)

indicators.note: the short form of Richard
RICK goes inside the other letters
re-creation: CRETE is created anew in a new order

blocks.note: Rick is a short form of Richard

annotation.surface: A man called Richard takes a holiday in Crete to unwind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recreation' reads as leisure, but split it as re-creation and it asks for the island's letters to be made again. 'Square' is the prepared central strip of a cricket field.
annotation.definitionFit: A cricketer plays on the square, the carefully tended middle of the cricket ground.

entries.clue: Improve education at the margins with opportunity initially missed (7)

indicators.note: keep only the edge letters of 'education'
points to the first letter of 'opportunity's' synonym
that first letter is left out

blocks.note: first and last letters of education
CHANCE without its first letter C

annotation.surface: Someone argues that schooling on the fringes can be improved where opportunities are lost.
annotation.walkthrough: Two trimmings in one clue: 'education' keeps only its outside, and CHANCE loses only its head.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean making something better.

entries.clue: Fancy reception’s fit for one with impossibly high standards (13)

indicators.note: a fancy version of the words is an elaborate rearrangement

annotation.surface: An elegant party is judged suitable for a guest who is never satisfied.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe S is part of the fodder: it supplies the S the answer needs.
annotation.definitionFit: A perfectionist refuses to accept anything short of flawless.

entries.clue: Sign of things to come found among some neighbours (4)

indicators.note: the answer is located among the letters of the next words

blocks.note: the tail of 'some' runs into the first letter of 'neighbours'

annotation.surface: A portent of the future turns up among the people next door.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between two words: s[OME N]eighbours.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a portent, good or bad, foretelling future events.

entries.clue: Environmentalist of a delicate nature gets permission to go ahead? (5,5)

blocks.note: a Green is an environmental campaigner
light = delicate, as in a light touch

annotation.surface: A gentle environmental campaigner is finally given approval for a project.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a figure of speech: a traffic signal standing for approval.
annotation.definitionFit: Getting the green light means being allowed to proceed, like a traffic signal.

entries.clue: A pair of notes by West Country banker in addition to a building (6)

blocks.note: a banker is a river (it has banks); the Exe flows through Devon

annotation.surface: Two banknotes are handed over by a West Country bank manager on top of a building deal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a crossword joke for a river. The West Country is south-west England, and the Exe runs through Exeter.
annotation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extra building or wing joined to a main one.

entries.clue: Fellow following with no end of interest method of extracting gas (8)

indicators.note: the last letter of 'interest' is taken away from the following word

blocks.clueFragment: following with no end of interest
blocks.note: TRACKING (following) minus T, the last letter of 'interest'

annotation.surface: A man trails along, bored, behind a new technique for getting gas out of the ground.
annotation.walkthrough: The T removed is the end of 'interest', not of 'following'. Fracking forces fluid into rock to release gas.
annotation.definitionFit: Fracking cracks underground rock with pressurised fluid to extract gas.

entries.clue: Manic set’s manipulated shades of meaning (9)

definitions.note: Semantics is a singular noun; the plural definition treats it as the nuances themselves.

indicators.note: the letters are handled and moved about

annotation.surface: A frantic group has twisted the finer points of what was said.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe S counts as a letter of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Semantics is the meaning of words, including their fine distinctions.

entries.clue: Random piece penned by a bishop on a railway (9)

indicators.note: BIT is enclosed within the bishop's letters
in a down clue, the first part sits on top of what follows

blocks.note: RR = Right Reverend, a bishop's title

annotation.surface: A stray fragment of writing turns up, composed by a bishop while travelling by train.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Penned' looks like writing, but it means enclosed, as in a sheep pen.
annotation.definitionFit: Arbitrary means random, not based on reason.

entries.clue: Hard material has support in confines of school (5)

indicators.note: TEE goes inside the other letters
the outer edges of 'school'

blocks.note: first and last letters of school
a golf tee supports the ball

annotation.surface: Tough building material has a supporting role within the school grounds.
annotation.walkthrough: TEE sits inside S…L: S(TEE)L.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the iron-and-carbon alloy is prized for its hardness.

entries.clue: Mention of wealthy people making projections (5)

indicators.note: to mention something is to say it, so the answer is how the word sounds

blocks.note: nobs is British slang for posh, rich people; the word you hear has a silent K in front

annotation.surface: Talk of the rich turns to their investment forecasts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nobs' is British slang for upper-class or wealthy people. 'Projections' looks like forecasts but means things that stick out.
annotation.definitionFit: Knobs are rounded lumps that project from a surface.

entries.clue: Grey person with no allegiance to either side (7)

definitions.text: person with no allegiance to either side

blocks.note: an adjective for a muted colour with no strong hue

blocks.clueFragment: person with no allegiance to either side
blocks.note: a noun for a country or person staying out of a conflict

annotation.surface: An unremarkable fence-sitter who backs neither camp.
annotation.walkthrough: Grey is both a neutral shade and a description of a dull, uncommitted person, so the two halves blur.
annotation.definitionFit: Neutral names both a muted colour and someone who takes no side.

entries.clue: Separate from friend left to wander overlooking lake (9)

indicators.note: the letters of FRIEND and LEFT roam into a new order
to overlook the lake is to leave out its L

blocks.note: l = lake, removed from the fodder

annotation.surface: Someone parts company with a friend who has gone off hiking with a view over a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Overlooking' paints a view of the lake; here it means ignoring, so one L drops out before the letters are shuffled.
annotation.definitionFit: Separate and different both mean distinct from one another.

entries.clue: One establishing an institution gets to be unsuccessful (7)

blocks.note: a noun: the person who sets up a school, charity or firm
a verb: to fail, originally of a ship filling and sinking

annotation.surface: The person who set up an organisation ends up failing.
annotation.walkthrough: The noun and the verb are spelt the same but have unrelated roots.
annotation.definitionFit: A founder establishes something; to founder is to collapse or fail.

entries.clue: Figure before ten has secure thing put in an alley? (7)

annotation.surface: A number just short of ten comes with a way of fastening something.
annotation.walkthrough: The alley is a skittle alley, where ninepins are set up to be knocked down; the question mark hints at that.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: these skittles are stood at the end of a skittle alley to be bowled at.

entries.clue: Twin has drink twice the normal measure (6)

blocks.note: what you order at a bar for two measures of spirits

annotation.surface: One twin orders a large whisky.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Has' works only as a joining word here, though the surface reads it as the twin having a drink.
annotation.definitionFit: A double is both a person's twin-like lookalike and a two-measure drink.

entries.clue: Finally catch leaders of heist unsettling new director in built-up area (4,4)

indicators.note: take the first letters of the next two words
D goes inside the built-up area

blocks.note: first letters of heist and unsettling
a town is a built-up area

annotation.surface: Police at last catch the ringleaders of a robbery who have been worrying a new manager in the city.
annotation.walkthrough: D goes after the T of TOWN: T(D)OWN. 'Unsettling' is not an anagram signal here; it just supplies its U.

entries.clue: Suave Republican graduate in a French café lately (6)

late in the word: its final letter

entries.clue: Heavily built liberal in part of Greater Manchester (5)

entries.clue: General journalist following Barbados in a storm (5-5)

ED comes after the rearranged letters

annotation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer; it is the adjective, meaning wide-ranging.
annotation.definitionFit: Broad-based means covering a wide range, which is general.

entries.clue: Chewy meat with time gone is ready to eat (4)

indicators.note: the T for time has disappeared

blocks.note: tripe, cow's stomach lining, is famously chewy

annotation.walkthrough: TRIPE loses its T to leave RIPE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for fruit or cheese that has matured enough to be eaten.

entries.clue: Favoured including unprofessional line in short drama (7)

entries.clue: Female with Gary in ground describing some old clothes? (7)
